# STEP 1 — Compiler archaeology (THE BLOCKER)

**Goal**: identify the exact avr-gcc version (and flags) that produced the V339
firmware (~2010-2015), then rebuild it on Mac ARM.

Without it, no function can match. With it, everything else follows.

## 1. Clues collected so far (to be refined)

| Clue | Observation | What it suggests |
|---|---|---|
| `__start` prologue | `clr r1 / out SREG / SP=0x045F / .data copy via lpm r0,Z+ / rjmp-skip` | classic avr-gcc crt, BUT custom `__bad_interrupt` (`jmp 0` = soft reset) → crt0 modified by the devs |
| Register allocation | e.g. `FUN_code_1b26`: `movw Z,R23R22 / movw X,R25R24 / lpm R0,Z+ / st X+,R0 / and R0,R0 / brbc` | gcc 4.x style (do/while loop optimized this way) |
| Multiplications | `mul` + `movw` used | avr5 target (ATmega162) |
| No libc calls | no `call` to div/memcpy | -Os + self-contained code |
| `ijmp` dispatch table | progmem table 0x54-0xE4 generated by the compiler | dense switch compiled to a table (version-dependent idiom!) |
| Fixed `jmp` vectors | 21 slots + custom bad | custom crt0/ld script |

## 2. Fingerprinting method

1. **Witness functions** (already matchable without the firmware): pick 6-8
   simple, self-contained functions:
   - `FUN_code_1b26` (0x364C, 14 B — NUL-terminated flash copy)
   - `FUN_code_1b18` / `1b1c` (16 B — helpers)
   - `FUN_code_019d` (cmd_T, 12 B: `lds/subi/sts/ret`)
   - `FUN_code_1b48` (24 B)
   - a `mul` loop (e.g. excerpt from 1527) to test loops
2. **Write plausible C** for each witness (independently, from the spec)
3. **Compile with the candidates**: avr-gcc 4.1.2, 4.3.3, 4.5.4, 4.7.4, 5.4,
   7.5, 9.5 (and GCC 3.4 if findable) × candidate options
   (`-Os`, `-Os -fomit-frame-pointer`, `-Os -mrelax` on/off, etc.)
4. **Compare the assemblies** byte by byte (this is the local score — the same
   diff as match.py, but byte by byte on these functions)
5. **Converge**: the version × flags that reproduces the MOST idioms wins;
   refine on the following functions

## 3. Where to find old compilers (Mac ARM → Docker)

avr-gcc 4.x binaries do not exist for arm64. Strategy:

- **Docker x86_64/arm64 Linux**: build avr-gcc N from the GCC sources
  (classic `--target=avr --enable-languages=c --disable-nls
  --with-dwarf2 ...` script) — decompilation projects use this approach
  (docker/dockcross). One image per candidate version.
- **Quick alternative**: fetch period binaries from archived distros
  (Debian/Ubuntu snapshots ~2010-2015 ship avr-gcc 4.x) and run them in a
  Linux container of the same era.
- **Search hints**: `avr-gcc 4.3 docker`, the repos of existing AVR matching
  projects (e.g. AVR game decompilations), historical avr-gcc images on
  `ghcr.io`.

## 4. Deliverable of this step

A `toolchain/` folder (in this project) containing:
- the Dockerfile / build script of the identified version,
- the exact flags,
- the reconstituted custom crt0 (see step 2),
- `verify-toolchain.sh`: compiles the witness functions and prints the match
  score ("8/8 witnesses identical").

## 5. Success / failure criterion

- ✓ **Success**: ≥ 6/8 witnesses byte-identical with a single version × flags
  combination → move on to step 2.
- ✗ **Failure** (after reasonable attempts): no combination comes close →
  "functional rewrite" mode (see METHODE-MATCHING.md §degraded mode).

## 6. Effort note

This is the most uncertain step of the project (hence the degraded mode).
Estimate: a few days — much of it Docker compile time. It needs NEITHER the CU
nor any further analysis: everything is in the binary we have and the witness
functions already understood.

### DISCOVERY #1 — the avr-libc is identified: **1.6.8**
The "strcpy_flash" witness (0x364C) = **`strcpy_P` of avr-libc 1.6.8**:
```
libc 1.6.8: fb 01 dc 01 05 90 0d 92 00 20 | 01 f4 (reloc) | 08 95
V339      : fb 01 dc 01 05 90 0d 92 00 20 | e1 f7 (resolved) | 08 95
```
→ **byte-for-byte match after branch resolution at link.**

### DISCOVERY #2 — 4 functions = avr-libc objects (match by construction)
| Address | Function | libc 1.6.8 object (m162 variant) |
|---|---|---|
| 0x364C | NUL-terminated flash copy | `strcpy_P` |
| 0x365A | EEPROM → SRAM copy | `__eerd_blraw_m162` (eeprom_read_block) |
| 0x367A | SRAM → EEPROM copy | `__eewr_block_m162` (eeprom_write_block) |
| 0x3690 | EEPROM byte write | `__eewr_r18_m162` (called by 0x367A ✓ consistent) |

⇒ These functions are not "rewritten": the source calls avr-libc 1.6.8 and
the linker supplies the objects — **match by construction** (the link order
must be replicated for the addresses, step 2).

### DISCOVERY #3 — THE CHIP IS AN ATmega16 (not 162!)
Ghidra display artifact: in/out operands are shown in data-space notation
(+0x20) — "out 0x0053" is actually out 0x33 = TCCR0 of the ATmega16.
Verified on the raw bytes (83 bf = out 0x33). The "ATmega162" identification
was wrong. Consequences:
- crt = standard crtm16.o of avr-libc 1.6.8: 21 jmp vectors, __bad_interrupt
  = jmp __vector_default, standard __init ⇒ vectors + crt0 + bad = MATCH BY
  CONSTRUCTION (like the libc functions).
- Layout confirmed: .vectors (0x00-0x53) → .progmem.gcc (0x54-0xE3 = the
  dispatch table generated by GCC for a switch) → .init/__start (0xE4) →
  __bad_interrupt (0x11E) → .text.
- build_bot.py switched to -mmcu=atmega16: image BIT-IDENTICAL (SHA 49e25766
  unchanged) — the BOT firmware stays valid as is.

### DISCOVERY #4 — Startup is 100% standard (PA-8, verified)
crtm16.o ↔ firmware comparison:
- `.init2` @0xE4: `11 24 1f be` + ldi SP (__stack=0x045F) + `de bf cd bf` = IDENTICAL ✓
- `.init4/.init6` (copy .data 0x60-0x6B from **0x36AC**, clear .bss 0x6C→0x417) ✓
- `.init9` @0x114: `call main` (0x351E) + `jmp exit` → **exit = 0x36A8** ✓
- `__bad_interrupt` @0x11E: `jmp __vector_default` → avr-libc's WEAK default
  = `__vectors` = 0x0000 → `0c 94 00 00` = SOFT RESET BY DESIGN ✓ (not custom!)
- **exit() @0x36A8 = `f8 94 ff cf` (cli + loop)** = 4 bytes — NOT the 6-byte
  version (cli+jmp _exit) of our libc.a 1.6.8 → they either defined their own
  `exit()`, or a slightly different libc. Micro-item to replicate in C:
  `void exit(void){ cli(); for(;;); }` (to be checked when matching).
- .data flash image @0x36AC (12 B) → then 0x36B8 = free area (our bots module!)

⇒ **The whole zone 0x0000-0x0122 + exit + .data = standard avr-libc/crt pieces**
(match by construction). Only these remain to rewrite/master: the .progmem
table 0x54-0xE3 (generated by GCC from their switch → will follow the matching
of the function that references it) + the devs' own functions.

### DISCOVERY #5 — the 0x00-0xE4 layout = STOCK tools
The avr5.x linker script of avr-libc 1.6.8 (with ld 2.20.1) defines:
`.text { *(.vectors) ; *(.progmem.gcc*) ; *(.progmem*) ; *(.trampolines) ; ...
; .init ; ... }` → EXACT order of the firmware:
- 0x0000: .vectors (crtm16.o — 21 jmp) ✓
- 0x0054: .progmem.gcc* = **the 140 B table generated by GCC** for the devs'
  switch (it will appear automatically when we match the function that
  references it — the compiler will generate it identically if version+flags OK)
- 0xE4: .init (crtm16.o) ✓
⇒ Nothing custom in the boot: everything comes from the stock toolchain.

### DISCOVERY #6 / PA-7 — THE COMPILER IS 4.7.x-ERA (mainline GCC, -Os)
Method: reconstruction of the dev functions as C witnesses + byte-exact scoring
(relocations masked) on period toolchains in containers.

**Coarse elimination:**
| version | TCO (terminal jmp) | mul ×16 | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1.0 / 4.2.2 / 4.3.3 / 4.5.3 | ✗ | ✗ (swap) | too old |
| **4.7.2 / 4.8.1 / 4.9.2** | **✓** | **✓** | **MATCH** |
| 9.5 | ✓ | ✗ (swap) | too recent |

**3 dev functions BYTE-EXACT at -Os on 4.7.2, 4.8.1 AND 4.9.2:**

| function | address | validated C idiom | score |
|---|---|---|---|
| init_serial | 0x01CE | `...; UBRRL=0x19; f01a6();` (terminal call → jmp) | 28/28 ✓ |
| set_timer2 | 0x0122 | `if (m != 2) { if (m == 4) {...} else v=3; } else { OCR2=0xFF; v=0x1B; } TCCR2=v;` (inverted test + nested if → merged store) | 30/30 ✓ |
| cmd_exclusion | 0x0232 | `volatile uint8_t *p; hi=p[1]; lo=p[0]-'0'; *(v)=lo+hi*16;` (VOLATILE pointer + hi loaded first) | 24/24 ✓ |

**DNA signatures (for all future reconstructions):**
1. `mul r25,r18` for ×16 on uint8_t → GCC ≥ 4.7 (4.5.3 and below do swap/andi)
2. TCO jmp on a terminal call → GCC ≥ 4.7 (4.5.3 and below do call+ret)
3. Accesses through a dev pointer stay `st Y` / `std Y+n` (no fold) if the pointer is local
4. The merged store of the branches (single `out`) = shape of an inverted nested if

  4.7-4.9 fold `buf[5]` (→sts 0x0122) and the call argument (→ldi constants) that
  the original keeps via Y (std Y+5 / movw) = 2 instructions. GCC 4.6.4 test in

### DISCOVERY #7 — Anatomy of the .progmem table (0x54-0xE3)
The 144 B table = **2 GCC jump tables** (.word entries = word addresses):
- **T1 = 0x54-0x95: 33 entries** = the main state machine (state 0x0218, 0..32)
  - T1[0]=0x1CA4, T1[1]=0x1CD0, T1[2]=0x1E5C, ... T1[32]=0x2948
- **T2 = 0x96-0xE3: 39 entries** = a 2nd switch (consumer outside the export)
- Dispatch verified: `subi Zlo,0xD6/sbci Zhi,0xFF` = -(0xFFD6) = +0x2A → (idx+0x2A)*2
  = 0x54 ✓; shared helper 0x3640 (GCC cross-jumping = will appear on its own
  when the switch functions are recompiled)
⇒ The C reconstruction of the state machine (0x1C76, ~3.7 KB) will regenerate T1
  AUTOMATICALLY if version/flags are right (4.7.2-4.9.2, -Os).

### DISCOVERY #8 — The 5 sub-switches of the state machine
Full raw scan (`avr-objdump -D -b binary`): 5 table dispatches + 1 ijmp:
- T1=0x54 (33), T2=0x96 (10), T3=0xAA (9), T4=0xBC (10), T5=0xD0 (10)
- dispatches @0x1CA0, 0x2168, 0x21F0, 0x23D0, 0x246A (all inside 0x1C76-0x2A4C)
- The 0x3640 helper (__tablejump2__ libgcc) will be regenerated automatically if
  the 5 switch functions match.
- Cycle table (0x62 SRAM) read at 0x2A6C (emitter) and 0x3022; main loop
  `jmp 0x1C76` @0x2E3C.
⇒ Priority reconstruction targets: 0x1C76 (state machine) then 0x2A4E
  (cycle emitter). These 2 functions = the core of the CU and of the bot interaction.

### DISCOVERY #10 — PRODUCTION RECONSTRUCTION (batches 1-3)
Production method (recon/): one C file per batch, symbolic globals/externs,
GCC 4.7.0 compilation (container `recon`) `-Os`, scoring `recon/score.py` (reloc mask).

**Batch 1: 3/5** ✓ cmd_T (0x033A), Timer2-overflow→tail (0x0EA2), capture arming (0x128C)
**Batch 2 (loops): 0/3** — micro residue: r24↔r25 allocation (envoyer_buffer, sum
0xB44) — noted as NEAR-match (1 register off, functionally identical)
**Batch 3: 3/4** ✓ 2-char param parser (0x024A), stop-timer (0xB02), PROG frame (0xB5C)

**Idioms confirmed by the matches:**
- `txbuf` buffer VOLATILE: the re-reads (0x24A re-reads txbuf[0] after the calls!)
- 16-bit stores by pairs: `*(uint16_t *)(p+n) = 0x3E20` (0x20,0x3E = " >")
  → the emitter writes PAIR by PAIR (high byte first = GCC's choice ✓)
- `somme(p, n)` (0xB44) = frame checksum (called by 0xB5C with n=19!)
- PROG frame = 6×" >" + [1,9,9,1,8,0,1] + checksum @+19 (to the tower!)
- m16 registers decoded: GIFR=0x3A, MCUCSR=0x34, TCCR0=0x33, TCNT0=0x32, OCR0=0x3C
- avr-libc cli()/sei() used directly (manual critical sections)

**TOTAL: 12 byte-exact dev functions** (+2 near-matches, 1 register off) + 5 by construction = **17/60**

### DISCOVERY #11 — THE COMPILER IS **GCC 4.8.1** (vanilla Debian/Ubuntu)
Discriminator: **loop unrolling**. The loop `for (p = 0x00E9; p < 0x0119; p += 6)`
(8 iterations, famous in 0x01A6):
- 4.7.0: **UNROLLED** into 8 × absolute sts = 54 bytes (10/40) ✗✗
- **4.8.1: loop kept = exactly 40 bytes (36/40)** ✓✓
- 5.4.0+Atmel: same as 4.8.1 (36/40)
⇒ **compiler = GCC 4.8.1 -Os** (container `gcc48`, gcc-avr 1:4.8.1-1 Debian jessie)
Consistent with EVERYTHING else: cmd_I ✓ cmd_version ✓ cmd_C ✓ (4.9.2 eliminated by cmd_C),
TCO ✓, mul ✓, symbolic ✓.

**State of recon on 4.8.1 (verified):**
- ✓ r6 (0x024A), r7 (0xB02), r8b (0xB5C) — confirmed identical to 4.7.0
- ✓ r1/r3/r5 (batch 1) — same codegen as 4.7.0 (matched)
- 36/40 r9 (0x01A6): residue = position of `ldi r25,1` (before/after cpi) + init
  of the 2 pointers — micro-scheduling
- 16/24 r2/r4 (envoyer_buffer/somme): residue = r24↔r25 allocation of the temporaries
- r8a (byte variant) discarded: the correct idiom = 16-bit stores `0x3E20`

**Production method (recon/):**
1. `recon/reconN.c`: reconstructions with symbolic `extern`s
2. Compilation: `avr-gcc -mmcu=atmega16 -Os -c` (container `recon` = 4.7.0, `gcc48` = 4.8.1)
3. Scoring: `recon/score.py dump.txt table.json` (masks the relocated bytes)
4. The addresses = left to the LINKER (symbolic method #9)

### DISCOVERY #12 — THE ISRs BY SUB-AGENT (verified at link!)
Batch entrusted to a general agent (recon_isr.c in toolchain/r2tmp/) — **3 byte-exact ISRs**:
| ISR | address | size | proof |
|---|---|---|---|
| isr_udre (USART_UDRE) | 0x064C | 92 B | ✓ scorer + **linked_dump = 92/92** |
| isr_capt (TIMER1_CAPT) | 0x0BA2 | 102 B | ✓ linked_dump = 102/102 |
| isr_int1 (INT1) | 0x0C08 | 102 B | ✓ linked_dump = 102/102 |

**The link test (link_isr.ld) = THE ultimate validation**: symbols placed at the real
addresses → binary identical to the firmware, zero diff. This is the proof that the
symbolic method clears the link hurdle!

**Idioms discovered by the agent (to reuse):**
1. POSITIVE `if (flag) {A} else {B}` (never the inverted form) — otherwise GCC reorders
   the blocks and breaks the layout (70/102 vs 102/102!)
2. Range fusion: `c != '#' && c != '$'` (adjacent!) → `subi 0x23 / cpi 2 / brcs`
   (ONE comparison instead of two!)
3. `d == div && d != 0` → `cpse r,r / rjmp / and/breq` (cpse for the 1st conjunct)
4. `(uint8_t)(t + 8 - last) >> 4` → `ldi 8/add/sub/swap/andi 0x0F` (÷16 in 1 swap)
5. Volatile ORDER enforced: the snapshot `uint8_t t = TCNT2;` must precede the
   `timeout = 5` write (hoisting of the `in` + r18 saved in the prologue)
6. `&= ~bit`: cbi if IO < 0x20 (UCSRB), in/andi/out if ≥ 0x20 (TIMSK/GICR)
7. `extern volatile uint8_t *rx_ptr;` = pointer to volatile → lds Zlo/Zhi + ld + re-lds/adiw/sts

### DISCOVERY #14 — THE FINAL PIN: avr-gcc 5.4.0+Atmel3.6.0 (Atmel Studio 7)
ISR agent #2 proved that **isr_rxc is IMPOSSIBLE on 4.8.1** (IRA never allocates
c→r24 / temporary→r18:r19, hence no subi/sbci nor push r19), but byte-exact on
4.9.2 AND 5.4.0+Atmel3.6.0. Yet cmd_C fails on 4.9.2. Contradiction resolved: **at
5.4.0+Atmel3.6.0, cmd_C matches with the TERNARY form** (cvd: `b = (src[1]=='1') ? 0x10 : 0x00`)
whereas the if/else form (which worked at 4.7/4.8) no longer matches. ⇒ the C forms
are pin-specific.

### CRITICAL NOTE (controller agent) — BRANCHES CAN ONLY BE PROVEN AT LINK
The scorer masks the bytes with a reloc (branches): `!=` vs `<` gives the same masked .o
but at link BRNE vs BRCS (d1 f7 vs d0 f3). Likewise the symbol+const compare (order of
`ldi r25,hi8` before cpi). ⇒ ALWAYS validate at link (the scorer = first filter only).
And: **C forms validated on one build hold only for that build** (0x01A6: the 4.8.1
form = 44 B at 5.4.0; cmd_C: if/else = 4.8.1, ternary = 5.4.0).

### DISCOVERY #15 — THE LAYOUT PUZZLE SOLVED (agent) + PIN CONFIRMED

### DISCOVERY #19 — BATCH 0x15xx-0x1Axx: 8 FUNCTIONS BYTE-EXACT AT LINK (verified)
f1524 (56), f155c (84), f15f8 (52), f16f2 (54), f1728 (408 !), f18c0 (50), f1a2c (48),
f1a5c (488 !) = 1240 B proven; near-matches: f162c (183/198), f18f2 (300/314).
**Major idioms (for the forms table):**
1. **Early extension**: `uint16_t idx = i;` used in ≥2 stores → `ldi r19,0` BEFORE the
   value computation (30/52 → 52/52!); stores = literal `volatile` accesses.
2. **IO outside the register zone**: literal mandatory (`*(volatile uint8_t*)0x5B=0;` →
   `out 0x3b,r1`; an extern would give `sts` ✗).
3. **Per-variable volatility = idiom**: w_92 volatile (lds×2+or+breq) vs w_d7
   non-volatile (sbiw/in-place decrement); some are non-volatile on purpose.
4. **Division signedness proven AT LINK**: `p[1]*10/15` (int promotion) → `mul` +
   __divmodhi4 (0x3618); with a (uint16_t) cast → __udivmodhi4 (2 bytes wrong: 0c1b vs f81a)!
5. **Lexical block order = code**: f1a5c — the `w_3d6=0x1E00` block must sit BETWEEN the
   2 arms (the rjmp jumps over it) → 420→488/488!
6. Checksum trap: `if (c != s) for(;;);` → `cpse/rjmp self` (ff cf at link).

### DISCOVERY #20 — THE LONG TAIL IS NOT THE SCHEDULER: 8 "NEAR" FUNCTIONS MATCH AT LINK
The earlier verdict ("residue = scheduler/IRA micro-decisions, invariant across all tools")
was wrong for the pinned compiler: `-fschedule-insns(2)` are off at -Os, nothing reorders
instructions after expand. What looked like scheduling was the order GCC fixes at expand
(+ TER, RTL loop-invariant motion, bb-reorder). Reading the GIMPLE/RTL dumps
(`-fdump-tree-optimized`, `-fdump-rtl-expand`) instead of trying C forms blindly solved
8 functions in one session (and a link-level check, `linkcheck.py`, caught the ones that
were only exact in the masked scorer):
| function | before | form that matched |
|---|---|---|
| 0x15B0 idle_timeout_service | todo | first try: `do { if (buttons_scan()) n = 0xFF; } while (n--);` |
| 0x0B44 sum_bytes | 16/24 | `for (uint8_t *q = p; q < p + n; q++)` — bound in the condition, sum=0 emitted first |
| 0x144C buttons_scan | 137/140 | `b = 0; if (!(PINC & 0x10)) b = 5;` instead of if/else (and `objdump -z`) |
| 0x0140 beep_queue_push | 88/102 | 16-bit counter var; 2nd store recomputes its base pointer -> `std Z+1` |
| 0x162C adc_sample_channels | 183/198 | index as `0x0402 + i + i`: two uses keep the zero-extend before the ADC reads (TER) |
| 0x12AE / 0x1344 rank_compute_a/b | 59/150, 50/152 (regs were already right: it was the LAYOUT) | indexed inner loop `u = &cars[j]`; a: leaves as one expression with one `rank--` |
| 0x18F2 update_frame_decode | 300/314 | 16-bit word loaded once (`t`) + `q = p + 4` INSIDE loop 1 with an empty asm barrier as 2nd use (RTL loop-invariant motion puts it after `i = 0`), sum loop on `p[4 + i]` |
Mechanisms worth remembering (details in method.md): statements before PHI copies; TER delays
single-use names to their use (two uses pin them); a second pointer walking a table makes
bb-reorder rotate the loop; branch polarity at link depends on how many `rank--` blocks exist;
ivopts keeps the counter of `for (i..) sum += q[i]` only if the base `q` is an expression
visible to the loop; RTL loop-invariant motion places hoisted values after the PHI copies.
